Repetitive Topics To Drill
  • Q1 is reliably search/adversarial search: minimax, game trees, BFS/DFS/iterative deepening and alpha-beta pruning.
  • Q2 is reliably evolutionary computation: GA design, representation, fitness, selection, crossover, mutation, diversity and search behaviour.
  • Q3 is reliably multi-agent systems/game theory: structured messages, auctions, prisoner's dilemma, Nash equilibrium, cooperation and coordination.
  • Q4 consistently contains explainability plus bio-inspired or contemporary AI. Explainability appears every year; ACO appears in all latest-three papers.

Exam / CA Strategy
  • Treat this as a predictable module, but do not rely on exact question repeats.
  • Prepare reusable answer frameworks for:
  • Minimax, alpha-beta pruning, BFS, DFS, iterative deepening, Monte Carlo Tree Search.
  • Genetic algorithm design: representation, fitness function, selection, crossover, mutation, diversity, graph colouring and NK landscapes.
  • Structured agent messages, auctions, prisoner's dilemma, dominant strategy, Nash equilibrium, coordination and cooperation.
  • Explainability, black-box models, artificial life, Ant Colony Optimisation, symbolic vs connectionist AI and LLM hallucination.
  • CA is worth 40%, so the assessment brief and coursework deadlines should be addressed early.
Short Learning Material

The following topic areas can be covered through short public tutorials, course catalogues, guided projects, or video chapters. Prefer material under 3 hours per topic.

  • AI search algorithms: BFS, DFS, uniform-cost, greedy best-first and A* with worked examples.
  • Adversarial search: minimax, alpha-beta pruning and game-tree evaluation.
  • Knowledge representation: propositional logic, first-order logic and rule-based inference.
  • Planning basics: state-space planning, STRIPS-style actions and goal decomposition.
  • Constraint satisfaction: backtracking, arc consistency and heuristics.
  • Reinforcement learning basics: Markov decision processes, value iteration and Q-learning.
  • AI ethics/safety overview: bias, explainability, accountability and deployment risks.
  • LLM reliability: hallucination, retrieval grounding, verification and uncertainty-aware responses.
